options: are evenly spaced across the region
are equally likely anywhere and independent of each other
questions.why: CSR has two assumptions: uniform intensity and independence. Random does not mean evenly spaced, and chance alone can still produce clusters and gaps.

questions.q: Crime incidents cluster near bars because bars are located downtown. This is mainly...
questions.why: First-order structure comes from intensity that varies with external drivers like the environment, policy or infrastructure.

questions.q: Trees that keep their distance from each other because they compete for light produce a regular pattern. That is...
questions.why: Second-order structure comes from interaction among the points themselves, either attraction or repulsion.

questions.q: What is the difference between intensity and density?
options: Intensity is the underlying rate of the process; density is the observed points per unit area, often used to estimate it
Intensity is always lower than density
questions.why: Intensity belongs to the process. Density, n divided by area, is what you can measure from the data.

questions.q: Why is the Poisson distribution used to model point patterns?
options: It is designed for counts of rare events spread over a continuous space
Points always form a bell curve
It only works for clustered patterns
questions.why: The chance of an event at any exact location is tiny, which fits the Poisson's rare-event counts.

options: intensity is constant and events attract each other
intensity varies across space, but events are still independent of each other
questions.why: Events respond to the environment but not to each other. That's why it can serve as a null model once first-order trends are accounted for.

questions.q: Why does the course use Monte Carlo simulation for most point pattern tests?
options: Many point pattern statistics don't have tractable variance formulas under CSR
It avoids the need for a null hypothesis
questions.why: Without a variance formula there is no classical test, so you simulate many CSR patterns and compare the observed statistic to them.

questions.q: The quadrat test results can change if you...
options: change the size or placement of the quadrats
change nothing; it always gives the same answer
questions.why: Quadrat tests are sensitive to quadrat size, placement and the shape of the study area.

questions.q: In kernel density estimation, the bandwidth controls...
options: how large the moving window is, and therefore how smooth the surface is
questions.why: A wider bandwidth spreads each point's influence further and gives a smoother surface. KDE is exploratory, with no formal test.

questions.q: An average nearest neighbor ratio R = 0.6 suggests...
questions.why: R below 1 means points are closer to their nearest neighbors than expected under CSR.

questions.q: Ripley's K-function differs from ANN because it...
options: only looks at the single nearest neighbor
summarizes clustering or regularity across a range of distances
questions.why: ANN catches very local structure. K counts all neighbors within distance d, for many values of d.

questions.q: Why do edge effects matter for the K-function?
options: Points near the boundary have neighbors outside the window that are missed, so counts are underestimated at larger distances
Edges make the map harder to read
questions.why: Edge corrections compensate for the part of each search circle that falls outside the study area.
